findings.label: Immediate-save path uncovered
findings.detail: Validation is gated on "first render", not "untouched", so clicking Save on a never-touched new connected system may persist a blank configuration if Appian does not re-render before saving. Design-time UX gap only: the runtime connection would fail and the integrations keep their own InputValidator.
findings.action: Add "open New > Connected System > MQTT Broker and save without touching anything; confirm it is rejected" to both deploy checklists (connected-system-descriptor-fix.md §8, connected-system-descriptor-fix-plan.md §5, connected-system-descriptor-fix-verification.md §7).

findings.label: Error-stickiness claim is too broad
findings.detail: connected-system-descriptor-fix.md §5 states the SDK error-cloning characteristic is "unreachable from a clean first render". It is unreachable only on the render-1 to render-2 transition; from render 2 onward errors exist, so a field flagged on render 2 and then filled may still show the stale message on render 3. The passing test only exercises the first transition. The behavior itself is correctly left unfixed as out of scope.
findings.action: Narrow the sentence in §5 and add a deploy observation: fix a field flagged on the second render and confirm its message clears.

findings.label: "or saves" is an unverified platform claim
findings.detail: README, the class Javadoc and the records all assert validation fires "the moment you interact with the form or save it". The interaction half follows from re-rendering; the save half is an assumption about platform behavior, the same uncertainty as finding 1.
findings.action: Either qualify the save half as unverified, or fold it into finding 1's deploy-checklist item.
